name: Jain Irrigation Systems Ltd
title: Jain Irrigation Systems Ltd - 500219 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 revenue up only ~4% to about INR1,800 crore after a March polymer price shock (~INR200-250 crore lost); management guides FY27 better and says ~INR600 crore operating cash flow, but ~INR40 crore reported PAT loss and large debt repayments due Sept and March 2027.

triggers.label: PE raw material up ~40% vs Feb peak
triggers.quote: those prices are about 40% up. They had gone up to 60% up, but they are now at around 40% level.

triggers.label: Q4 revenue short by INR200-250 crore
triggers.quote: the entire reduction, about INR200 crores, INR250 crores is linked to this pricing shock in March.

triggers.label: FY27 PAT positive plan
triggers.quote: For FY '27, right, our plan right now is to be PAT positive.

triggers.label: Govt receivables cut INR80 crore in Q4
triggers.quote: there was some movement in this particular quarter where some INR80 crores were reduced in January to March from the government project receivables.

summary.headline: Jain Irrigation Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 4% to INR1,800 crore and EBITDA about 7%, but a March raw-material shock cost an estimated INR200-250 crore of quarterly sales.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was about INR1,800 crore versus about INR1,750 crore a year earlier, with Hi-Tech up about 8%, Plastics down slightly and Agro Processing up about 6%. Consolidated EBITDA grew about 7% and margin rose to 13.2% from 12.8%, with Hi-Tech margin at 19.8% versus 17.5%. Management attributed the shortfall versus its earlier expectation to a polymer price spike in late February to March that made farmers postpone purchases. Reported PAT was negative at about INR40 crore, driven by one-time tax and non-cash items; management cited an adjusted PAT of about INR133 crore. Management said the debt repayment due in September and March FY27 will be met from internal accruals, with refinancing and equity as backups.

segments.name: Hi-Tech (drip irrigation, tissue culture, solar agri pumps)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up about 8% and EBITDA up about 22%, margin 19.8%; FY26 revenue up over 20%. Domestic business grew about 12% and retail about 13% (target above 15%).

segments.name: Plastics (pipes and plastic sheets)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue slightly down and EBITDA up 3.3%, margin 10.2%; FY26 revenue up only 2.4% and EBITDA declined. Pipes did not grow in FY26 and are expected to grow in FY27; overseas sheet business doing well.

segments.name: Agro Processing / Food
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up about 6% but EBITDA declined; FY26 revenue above INR2,000 crore (up 9%) and EBITDA up about 9%. UK food revenue rose to GBP68 million from GBP60 million, with cost headwinds; beverage lines started in Q4.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 exports about INR455 crore versus INR500 crore, down about 10%.

guidance_outlook: Management plans to be PAT positive (after adjustments) in FY27, and says it expects FY27 to be better than FY26 on revenue, margins, cash flow and balance sheet.

Standalone operating cash flow expected to rise from about INR350 crore to INR750-800 crore in FY27, helped by about INR450 crore of government receivables and about INR150 crore of government benefits.
Management expects the second half of Q4 to be better than the first and July onwards to be better, unless another price shock occurs.
Beverage: three more lines under discussion for FY27 investment. Tomato processing plant with a Japanese partner expected to start around January.
Management declined to give numeric FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance, citing uncertainty.
Management said a food IPO is not expected in the first half of FY27; it will reassess in the second half.
capex_capacity: Beverage bottling: about INR140 crore invested over December and March quarters; two lines started in February and March, with about INR27-28 crore revenue before end-March. Three more lines are under discussion, with investment possibly in December-January.
Tamil Nadu land asset sale: MoU signed; management expects closure within weeks to a month or two. Amount not disclosed.
Alwar plant in Rajasthan is being expanded to grow pipe sales in North India.
Management says the first big government projects are complete, but final milestones remain pending.
demand_pricing: PVC and polyethylene prices rose by more than 50% within about 20 days (polyethylene about 60%) between 20 February and 25 March. Late April and early May, PVC fell to about 10% above February levels, while polyethylene remained about 40% higher.
Farmers postponed purchases in March and April; management says PVC pipe demand has since returned. Monsoon is expected to be below normal, which management sees as supportive of irrigation demand.

Management says about INR200-250 crore of Q4 revenue was lost to the March shock; standalone Q4 revenue would otherwise have been about INR1,250 crore versus about INR1,000 crore, with EBITDA about INR25 crore higher.
Export prices for farmers' produce (banana, onion, grapes) fell during the conflict-related shock; management says prices have since stabilised.

FY26 drip sales by region: Maharashtra about INR700 crore, South four states about INR400 crore, West about INR250 crore, North about INR88 crore (up from INR75 crore), East about INR107 crore (up from INR60 crore), North East about INR100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will debt repayment be serviced given limited standalone cash flow, and what restructuring or fundraising backups exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects standalone operating cash flow to rise from about INR350 crore to INR750-800 crore, plus about INR150 crore of government benefits, and expects to repay most of the debt from internal accruals. Backups include refinancing and equity. A smaller amount is due in September and the majority in March. Management says the Tamil Nadu land sale is near closure and that it will provide more clarity in July.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Tamil Nadu asset sale near closure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an MoU is signed and closure is expected within a couple of weeks to a month, though it did not give a value or a firm date.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company turn PAT positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan is to be PAT positive for FY27 on a reported basis. FY26 reported PAT was about minus INR40 crore; adjusted PAT was about INR133 crore after one-time and non-cash items.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress in beverages and bottling, and what revenue is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Two lines started in February and March with about INR27-28 crore revenue before end-March. Three more lines are under discussion. UK food EBITDA is expected to recover in FY27 as one-off cost headwinds fade.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 revenue short of expectations by about INR200-250 crore, and where was it lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the shortfall to the March raw-material price shock, which led farmers to delay purchases, and to weaker farm-gate prices from reduced exports. It said margins were held, and the lost revenue would otherwise have added about INR25 crore of EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why is drip irrigation adoption weaker in North India and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said farmers in North have lower groundwater costs and free power, so water conservation matters less. North drip sales rose about 20% to INR88 crore in FY26. Management expects adoption to grow over the next 5-7 years as dealers expand and farmers shift to value-added crops.

risks_watch: Debt servicing: additional obligations fall due in September and March FY27, and the company depends on government receivable collections, the Tamil Nadu asset sale and possible refinancing or equity.
Polymer price volatility: PVC and polyethylene remain elevated and could spike again, and management says the outlook is contingent on no new price shock.
Food business: UK and US overseas operations had challenges, with management expecting these to ease in FY27; beverage ramp-up and the tomato plant timeline are unproven.
Exports fell about 10% in FY26 to INR455 crore, with trade and tariff uncertainty flagged.
Reported PAT remains negative, and FY27 PAT positivity is only a plan.
Management did not provide quantitative FY27 guidance; watch the July update on refinancing and asset sale closure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term structure and debt repayment, but cautious on near-term outlook, repeatedly qualifying FY27 with uncertainty and declining to give numbers. Answers on debt backups were less specific than the reassurances, and the company relied on the claimed Tamil Nadu sale and government receivables.
key_quotes: And PVC is down to about 10% compared to where it was in February.
So the entire reduction, about INR200 crores, INR250 crores is linked to this pricing shock in March.
And we feel that company would be able to generate adequate internal accruals to be able to take care of that matter.
